newsitem.title: MEXICO: Four consortia vying for Mexico Tampico natgas bid.
newsitem.headline: Four consortia vying for Mexico Tampico natgas bid.

text.p: Four consortia turned in technical bids to compete for natural gas distribution rights in the Tampico, Altamira and Ciudad Madero region in Mexico's northeastern Tamaulipas state, the Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Tuesday.
A total of 10 companies joined forces to line up for the regional concession, also known as the Rio Panuco zone.

A slew of petrochemical firms and an industrial corridor in the region have made the zone particularly competitive, analysts said. The region is also attractive because of its proximity to the United States, allowing the winning bidder to import natural gas for distribution.
The CRE said the four consortium that turned in bids were:
--Mexico's Grupo Mexicano de Desarollo ; Mexico's B.C. Gas and Shell Oil Co
--Mexico's Compania Mexicana de Gas and Enserch de Mexico, a division of Enserch Corp
--France's GDF International ; Mexigas and Mexico's Bufete Industrial
--NorAm Energy de Mexico, a division of NorAm Energy Corp, and Mexico's Corporacion Gutsa
This latest list of bidders is half of the original group of interested companies. Among those that dropped out of the running were Repsol Mexico, of Spain's Repsol, and U.S. KN Energy Inc..
A final decision on the winning bidder of the 30-year concession is expected by Sept. 11, the CRE said.
